ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The cross section of a resistor made of a conducting medium is shown in the figure. The resistivity of the conducting medium is ρ, and it is made into the shape of a hemispherical shell layer with inner and outer radii respectively a and b (the shaded part in the figure). A spherical electrode with radius a and negligible resistance is embedded at the center of the sphere of the conducting medium to become one lead-out electrode, and a layer of metal film with negligible resistance is plated on the outer spherical shell of the conducting medium to become another electrode. Let the resistance of this resistor be R. Among the four expressions for R given below, only one is reasonable. You may not be able to solve for R, but you can, through certain physical analysis, judge the reasonableness of the following expressions. According to your judgment, the reasonable expression for R should be (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The resistivity of the conducting medium is ρ, and its geometrical shape is a hemispherical shell layer with inner radius a and outer radius b. At the center of the sphere there is a spherical inner electrode with radius a and negligible resistance, and the outer surface is plated with a metal film with negligible resistance as the outer electrode. Find the expression for the resistance R between the two electrodes of this hemispherical-shell conductor.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The resistivity of the conducting medium is ρ, and its geometrical shape is a hemispherical shell layer with inner radius a and outer radius b. At the center of the sphere there is a spherical inner electrode with radius a and negligible resistance, and the outer surface is plated with a metal film with negligible resistance as the outer electrode. Find the expression for the resistance R between the two electrodes of this hemispherical-shell conductor.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a cross-sectional schematic diagram. The gray shaded part is the conducting medium, in the shape of the lower half of a hemispherical shell layer; the center is marked O, and near the center there is a white circular inner electrode, whose radius is marked a; outside the gray region is the outer hemispherical surface with radius b, and on the outer surface there is a metal film/lead-out terminal; the upper and lower lead wires are marked with current I. It can be seen from the figure that the inner electrode and the outer hemispherical electrode respectively correspond to spherical boundaries with radii a and b. Reasoning: The resistance of the inner electrode and the metal film on the outer surface can both be ignored, so the spherical surface of inner radius a and the hemispherical surface of outer radius b can be regarded as equipotential surfaces. According to the symmetry of the hemispherical shell, the current is distributed radially from the inner electrode near the center of the sphere toward the outer hemispherical surface. Take a thin hemispherical shell with radius r and thickness dr as a resistance element; the cross-sectional area through which the current passes is the area of this hemispherical surface, S=2πr^2. Thus the elemental resistance is dR=ρdr/S=ρdr/(2πr^2). These thin hemispherical shells are connected in series along the radial direction, integrating from r=a to r=b: R=∫_a^b ρdr/(2πr^2)=ρ/(2π)[-1/r]_a^b=ρ/(2π)(1/a-1/b)=ρ(b-a)/(2πab).
